# Working with awf
# Working with awf

awf owns this project's generated contributor workflow, documentation, and root agent guide. Edit committed `.awf/` sources and convention parts, then run `./awf render` and keep generated outputs with the source change.

This guide covers day-to-day source and render handling. [Workflow](workflow.md) owns effort lifecycle and model selection, [Debugging](debugging.md) owns recovery, and the [configuration reference](config-reference.md) owns configuration semantics.


<!-- awf:edit commands: default; create .awf/parts/working-with-awf/commands.md to override -->
## Daily commands

- `awf init`: scaffold `.awf/` and render the standard workflow footprint into the current project.
- `./awf render`: re-render managed artifacts from `.awf/` and update `.awf/awf.lock`.
- `./awf check`: confirm the rendered tree and repository checks are clean.
- `./awf upgrade`: apply pending configuration migrations and re-render after upgrading awf.
- `./awf config [<key-or-var>]`: inspect effective configuration.

Use the repository `./awf` wrapper for local commands. For workflow and effort commands, see
[Workflow](workflow.md); for a command refusal or failed upgrade, see
[Debugging](debugging.md).

<!-- awf:edit config-and-overrides: default; create .awf/parts/working-with-awf/config-and-overrides.md to override -->
## Config and overrides

Configuration lives in `.awf/config.yaml`, artifact sidecars, and convention parts. The
[configuration reference](config-reference.md) is the single home for every key and for
placeholder semantics. A convention part replaces one declared section; use its
`awf:edit` pointer to find the source, then render and check.

Generated files are awf-owned. An `awf:edit` pointer names a convention-part source; a topic
page names its metadata and claim part. Local documents are the exception: edit only their body
after the `awf:edit-in-place` pointer through end-of-file. See the [documentation standard](doc-standard.md) for
authorship rules.

<!-- awf:edit sync-and-drift: default; create .awf/parts/working-with-awf/sync-and-drift.md to override -->
## Keeping in sync

After editing `.awf/`, run `./awf render` and then `./awf check`. Commit regenerated outputs and
`.awf/awf.lock` with their sources. If check reports drift, change the owning source and render;
do not repair a generated output by hand.

<!-- awf:edit upgrading: default; create .awf/parts/working-with-awf/upgrading.md to override -->
## Upgrading awf

From the project root, use the rendered upgrade script when bootstrap is enabled:

```sh
bash .awf/upgrade.sh
```

Then inspect the changed generated outputs, run `./awf check`, and commit the source, output, and
lock updates together. Upgrades rename retained authored skill overrides to the four fixed AWF
identities only when ownership and collision checks permit it. Content AWF cannot prove it owns
blocks mutation rather than being overwritten, moved, or copied aside. If an upgrade fails, inspect
the reported paths and Git diff, correct the blocker, and rerun it. See [Debugging](debugging.md).
